categories.name: Skull
categories.description: Bones of the cranium and face that protect the brain and support the face.

categories.name: Brain
categories.description: Major divisions of the central nervous system inside the cranial cavity.

categories.name: Eye & Orbit
categories.description: The eyeball, the muscles that move it, and the optic nerve.

categories.name: Muscles
categories.description: Muscles of facial expression, mastication and the tongue.

categories.name: Hand Skeleton
categories.description: The 27 bones of the wrist, palm and fingers.

categories.name: Body Skeleton
categories.description: The axial skeleton (spine, rib cage, pelvis) and the bones of the arms and legs.

structures.name: Frontal bone
structures.description: The broad bone forming the forehead, the roofs of the eye sockets and the front of the cranial vault.
structures.function: Protects the frontal lobes of the brain and shapes the forehead and upper orbits.

structures.name: Parietal bones
structures.description: A pair of curved plates forming the sides and roof of the cranium, meeting in the midline at the sagittal suture.
structures.function: Enclose and protect the upper and lateral surfaces of the brain.

structures.name: Occipital bone
structures.description: The bone at the back and base of the skull containing the foramen magnum, through which the brainstem joins the spinal cord.
structures.function: Protects the back of the brain and articulates with the first cervical vertebra to allow nodding.

structures.name: Temporal bones
structures.description: Paired bones at the sides of the skull that house the middle and inner ear and form part of the jaw joint.
structures.function: Protect the hearing and balance organs and provide the socket for the temporomandibular joint.

structures.name: Sphenoid bone
structures.description: A butterfly-shaped bone at the centre of the skull base that links the cranial and facial skeleton.
structures.function: Forms part of the orbits and skull base and cradles the pituitary gland in the sella turcica.

structures.name: Ethmoid bone
structures.description: A light, sponge-like bone between the eye sockets that forms part of the nasal cavity.
structures.function: Separates the nasal cavity from the brain and transmits the olfactory nerve fibres.

structures.name: Zygomatic bones
structures.description: The cheekbones, forming the prominence of the cheek and the outer rim of each eye socket.
structures.function: Shape the cheeks, protect the eyes and give origin to the masseter and zygomatic muscles.

structures.name: Maxillae
structures.description: The paired upper jawbones that hold the upper teeth and form the floor of the orbits and much of the hard palate.
structures.function: Anchor the upper teeth, support the nose and cheeks and separate the mouth from the nasal cavity.

structures.name: Nasal bones
structures.description: Two small oblong bones forming the bridge of the nose.
structures.function: Support the upper part of the nose; the lower nose is shaped by cartilage that is not shown.

structures.name: Lacrimal bones
structures.description: The smallest bones of the face, located in the inner wall of each orbit.
structures.function: Contain the groove for the tear sac that drains tears into the nose.

structures.name: Palatine bones
structures.description: L-shaped bones at the back of the nasal cavity forming the rear of the hard palate.
structures.function: Complete the roof of the mouth and the floor of the nasal cavity.

structures.name: Vomer
structures.description: A thin, plough-shaped bone forming the lower back part of the nasal septum.
structures.function: Divides the nasal cavity into left and right passages.

structures.name: Inferior nasal conchae
structures.description: Scroll-shaped bones projecting from the side walls of the nasal cavity.
structures.function: Increase the surface area of the nose to warm and humidify inhaled air.

structures.name: Upper teeth
structures.description: The permanent maxillary teeth: incisors, canines, premolars and molars set in the upper jaw.
structures.function: Cut, tear and grind food against the lower teeth and help shape speech sounds.

structures.name: Mandible
structures.description: The lower jawbone, which supports the lower teeth and participates in chewing and speech.
structures.function: The only movable bone of the skull; it hinges and glides at the temporomandibular joints to open and close the mouth.

structures.name: Lower teeth
structures.description: The permanent mandibular teeth set in the lower jaw.
structures.function: Move with the mandible to bite and chew against the upper teeth.

structures.name: Left cerebral hemisphere
structures.description: The left half of the cerebrum, its folded cortex divided into frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes.
structures.function: Controls movement and sensation of the right side of the body and, in most people, language.

structures.name: Right cerebral hemisphere
structures.description: The right half of the cerebrum, connected to the left hemisphere by the corpus callosum.
structures.function: Controls movement and sensation of the left side of the body and contributes strongly to spatial attention.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.description: The 'little brain' tucked beneath the occipital lobes at the back of the skull.
structures.function: Coordinates movement, balance, posture and the timing of motor skills.

structures.name: Brainstem
structures.description: The midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata connecting the cerebrum and cerebellum to the spinal cord.
structures.function: Regulates breathing, heart rate and consciousness and relays signals between brain and body.

structures.name: Ventricular system
structures.description: A set of connected fluid-filled cavities deep within the brain.
structures.function: Produces and circulates cerebrospinal fluid, which cushions the brain and removes waste.

structures.name: Eyeball (sclera)
structures.description: The tough white outer coat of the eye, about 24 mm across, continuous with the clear cornea at the front.
structures.function: Maintains the shape of the eye and provides attachment for the muscles that move it.

structures.name: Cornea
structures.description: The transparent dome at the front of the eye.
structures.function: Provides most of the eye's focusing power.

structures.name: Iris
structures.description: The coloured ring of muscle surrounding the pupil.
structures.function: Adjusts pupil size to control how much light enters the eye.

structures.name: Lens
structures.description: A flexible, transparent structure behind the iris.
structures.function: Changes shape to fine-tune focus for near and distant objects.

structures.name: Optic nerves
structures.description: Cables of over a million nerve fibres leaving the back of each eye and passing through the optic canal of the sphenoid bone.
structures.function: Carry visual information from the retina to the brain.

structures.name: Extraocular muscles
structures.description: Six muscles per eye (four rectus and two oblique) plus the eyelid-raising levator palpebrae superioris.
structures.function: Rotate the eyes precisely so both point at the same target; the eyeball model rotates with your tracked gaze.

structures.name: Extrinsic tongue muscles
structures.description: The genioglossus and hyoglossus, which anchor the tongue to the mandible and hyoid bone.
structures.function: Protrude, retract and depress the tongue during speech and swallowing.

structures.name: Frontalis (schematic)
structures.description: The frontal belly of the occipitofrontalis, a thin vertical sheet beneath the forehead skin.
structures.function: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead.

structures.name: Orbicularis oculi (schematic)
structures.description: A ring of muscle encircling each eye within the eyelids and around the orbit.
structures.function: Closes the eyelids for blinking and squinting and helps drain tears.

structures.name: Zygomaticus major (schematic)
structures.description: A strap-like muscle running from the cheekbone to the corner of the mouth.
structures.function: Draws the corner of the mouth up and out — the main smiling muscle.

structures.name: Buccinator (schematic)
structures.description: A thin, deep muscle forming the wall of the cheek between the upper and lower jaws.
structures.function: Presses the cheek against the teeth to keep food between them and helps blow air out.

structures.name: Masseter (schematic)
structures.description: A thick, powerful muscle from the zygomatic arch to the angle of the mandible.
structures.function: The prime chewing muscle: elevates the mandible to close the jaw.

structures.name: Orbicularis oris (schematic)
structures.description: The sphincter-like muscle encircling the mouth within the lips.
structures.function: Closes and purses the lips for speech, eating and expression.

structures.name: Temporalis (schematic)
structures.description: A fan-shaped muscle covering the side of the skull above the ear, converging on the coronoid process of the mandible.
structures.function: Elevates and retracts the mandible to close the jaw.

structures.name: Carpal bones
structures.description: Eight small bones in two rows forming the wrist: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate.
structures.function: Allow the wrist to flex, extend and tilt while transmitting forces from the hand to the forearm.

structures.name: Metacarpals
structures.description: Five long bones forming the palm, numbered I (thumb) to V (little finger).
structures.function: Form the framework of the palm; their heads are the knuckles.

structures.name: Phalanges
structures.description: The 14 finger bones: proximal, middle and distal phalanges for each finger, and two phalanges for the thumb.
structures.function: Their hinge joints let the fingers bend to grip, pinch and manipulate objects.

structures.name: Rib cage
structures.description: Twelve pairs of curved ribs joined to the spine at the back and, through costal cartilages, to the sternum at the front.
structures.function: Protects the heart and lungs and moves with every breath to expand the chest.

structures.name: Sternum
structures.description: The flat breastbone in the centre of the chest, made of the manubrium, body and xiphoid process.
structures.function: Anchors the ribs and clavicles and shields the heart.

structures.name: Vertebral column
structures.description: The spine: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic and 5 lumbar vertebrae resting on the sacrum.
structures.function: Supports the head and trunk, allows bending and twisting, and protects the spinal cord.

structures.name: Clavicles
structures.description: The collarbones: S-shaped struts between the sternum and each shoulder blade.
structures.function: Hold the shoulders away from the trunk so the arms can swing freely.

structures.name: Scapulae
structures.description: Triangular shoulder blades lying against the back of the rib cage.
structures.function: Provide the shoulder socket and attachments for the muscles that move the arm.

structures.name: Pelvis (hip bones)
structures.description: The paired hip bones, each formed by the fused ilium, ischium and pubis, joined to the sacrum.
structures.function: Transfers body weight to the legs, holds the hip sockets and protects pelvic organs.

structures.name: Humerus
structures.description: The long bone of the upper arm, from the shoulder to the elbow.
structures.function: Lever for shoulder and elbow movements; its head forms the ball of the shoulder joint.

structures.name: Radius and ulna
structures.description: The two parallel bones of the forearm between the elbow and the wrist.
structures.function: Let the forearm rotate (palm up / palm down) and transmit forces from the hand.

structures.name: Femur
structures.description: The thigh bone: the longest and strongest bone in the body.
structures.function: Carries body weight from the hip to the knee and drives walking and running.

structures.name: Tibia, fibula and patella
structures.description: The shin bone (tibia), the slender fibula beside it, and the kneecap (patella).
structures.function: The tibia bears weight; the patella improves the leverage of the thigh muscles at the knee.

structures.name: Foot bones
structures.description: 26 bones: seven tarsals (including the talus and heel bone), five metatarsals and fourteen toe phalanges.
structures.function: Form flexible arches that support body weight and absorb impact during walking.
